To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the fault detection problem is not solvable in general, 2) the fault diagnosis problem is not solv-able in general and 3) the fault correction problem is not sol-vable in general.

The design of self-checking circuits requires the use of testable components and that the testability of a component is related to the number and location of its faults that can be detected by a given set of test vectors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (1) fault detection in combinational circuits; (2) fault detection in sequential circuits; (3) fault detection in systems with memory; (4) test generation and fault detection in systems without memory; (5) fault detection in self-checking circuits; (6) testable and/or fault-tolerant systems; (7) self-checking systems; and (8) self-checking and testable systems.
the study of methods for detecting faults and their impact on the design of digital circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no general methods to detect all possible faults in a circuit.
the design of testable and/or fault tolerant systems is an open problem and that the methods presented here are only the first steps towards its solution.
fault detection is not only a theoretical problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a methodology for the design of digital systems which is based on the detection of the faults that can be present in the circuits.
the design of digital circuits is not an isolated problem but a part of the design of a complete system.
we have developed a methodology for the design of testable circuits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of self-checking circuits requires the use of a test set that can detect all possible faults.
the design of self-checking circuits is a difficult task.
the fault detection problem is an NP-complete problem, and that the problem becomes even more complicated when the circuit is modified in order to make it easily testable.
